scope: Phase B readiness for optional nodalmerge-tools split (headless + cli)
preconditions: Tier 1/Tier 2 parity gates are identified in CI/workflow inventory

required_readiness_checks.description: Dependency boundary map exists for headless/cli consumption of core crates
CI contract defined between core repo and tools repo (version compatibility lane)
Parity acceptance artifacts remain in core and are referenced by tools workflows
Release packaging/docs ownership split is documented

non_blocking_followups: Query control-plane parity decision lane for host/server

ci_workflows_candidates: .github/workflows/dotnet-peerlocal-smoke.yml (retain in core if host tests remain core-owned)
scripts_candidates: scripts/integration-smoke.ps1 (or split into core-smoke + tools-smoke variants)

crate_dependencies_from_tools_to_core: nodalmerge-server (only for vector test harnesses if retained)
protocol_contract_source_of_truth: core protocol types + host/core mapping contracts in core repo
tools repo consumes but does not redefine protocol envelopes

version_pin_contract_v1.strategy: tools repo pins to tagged core release (no floating main for release lanes)
core_release_inputs: git tag vX.Y.Z in core repo
published crates/packages for required core surfaces

tools_pin_examples.cargo: core crates pinned to =X.Y.Z for release branches; patch lanes may use git rev during development
tools_pin_examples.dotnet_native_artifacts: tools smoke lanes consume core-produced native artifacts by matching version tag

required_ci: tools repo CI against latest released core tag
periodic canary CI against core main (non-blocking)
compatibility_lane.failure_policy: release-blocking if released-tag compatibility fails; canary failures create follow-up issues

core_repo_required_jobs.purpose: Rust host runtime <-> .NET host runtime parity smoke
legacy Rust integrated server compatibility smoke
minimum_checks: known bounded deltas are documented in acceptance artifacts

core_repo_required_jobs.purpose: produce release candidate artifacts consumed by tools repo
minimum_checks: versioned crates/packages available for tools dependency set
artifact manifest published with exact version pins
headless vectors against pinned core version
CLI workflow vectors against pinned core version
integration smoke script runs with pinned core artifacts

tools_repo_required_jobs.purpose: early warning lane against core main branch
minimum_checks: auto-open issue on regression with failing job links

cross_repo_trigger_contract.core_release_tag_event: tools repo compatibility workflow auto-triggers on new core release tag
cross_repo_trigger_contract.core_rc_event: optional pre-release trigger for RC validation
cross_repo_trigger_contract.tools_pr_gate: tools PRs must pass pinned-core lane; canary lane advisory only

pass_fail_policy.exception_process: Any blocker waiver requires explicit acceptance artifact note with owner and expiry date.

evidence_requirements: Core release notes include artifact versions consumed by tools
Tools release notes include tested core version(s)
Acceptance artifact references CI run IDs for both repos

source_of_truth.rule: Tools repo may reference but must not fork or redefine parity acceptance artifacts.

tools_reference_rules.rule: Every tools release notes entry must include tested core version tag and links to relevant core acceptance artifacts.
Tools CI summaries must emit artifact references as immutable links (core commit SHA + file path).
If tools behavior diverges from core parity expectation, create a new core acceptance artifact documenting bounded delta and owner.

artifact_naming_policy.collision_rule: Tools must not create files in core-owned acceptance namespaces.

migration_sequence: Step 1: Keep existing acceptance artifacts in core unchanged.
Step 2: Add tools workflow links to core artifacts (no copy).
Step 3: After split, verify links by core SHA in tools CI output.
Step 4: Add one post-split acceptance artifact in core confirming reference integrity.
completion_criteria: Tools workflows reference core artifacts by immutable links.
No duplicate parity acceptance JSON files exist in tools repo.
At least one post-split link-integrity artifact is recorded in core.

core_repo_owns: Rust core/host crates and wrappers publishing flow
.NET host native/runtime packages and host composition packaging
tools_repo_owns: tools-oriented smoke script packaging and release notes
packaging_ownership.shared_handoff_rule: Tools release must consume published core artifacts by explicit version; no implicit local rebuild of core release assets in tools release lane.

core_repo_docs: integrator contract docs (metrics schema, capability model, rejection taxonomy)
tools_repo_docs: tools-specific migration notes and release playbooks
docs_ownership.cross_link_policy: Tools docs link to core contract docs; core docs link to tools operational docs where relevant without duplicating content.

release_handoff_checklist_v1.item: Core release tag and artifact manifest published
Tools release pins exact core versions and records them in release notes
Cross-repo CI compatibility lane green for pinned versions
Post-release acceptance artifact records handoff success/fail with run IDs

completion_criteria: Ownership boundaries for packaging and docs are explicit and non-overlapping.
Release handoff checklist is executable and referenced by both repos.
A post-split packaging/docs artifact is recorded in core acceptance.

core_repo_owners: acceptance artifacts and parity policy docs
tools_repo_owners: headless runtime packaging and operator UX

notes: This artifact is intentionally planning-only; update statuses as Phase B tasks execute.
Map/version contracts are first-pass draft and should be finalized before TOOLS-SPLIT-002 gate is marked complete.
